thread:
nora: Small docs bug: openapi examples for /embeddings show request field 'input' as a single string, but our API accepts array-of-strings for batch. The example confuses users trying to batch. Can we add a batch example and clarify the request shape?

izzy: Good catch. The schema is correct but the example is single-item. I'll add a second example file embeddings.batch.json and update the docs page to show both single and batch request samples.

ben: Also update SDK snippets to show batch usage for python and js - quick one-liners. I'll do python, izzy can do JS.

ci-bot: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/1310 - adds batch example + snippets. Preview link: https://deploy.preview.redwood.ai/preview/1310.

ci-bot: Preview shows the new batch examples but the openapi validator flagged the examples file with a type mismatch: array of strings vs string in a few references. Need to adjust the example schema refs.

izzy: Fix pushed to reference the correct schema component (EmbeddingsRequest). Also added a short note in the page: "Tip: prefer batch requests (arrays) for higher throughput".

ben: Updated python snippet to `client.embeddings.create({ model: ..., input: ["a","b"] })` and added a one-liner showing how to map ids.

ci-bot: CI passed ✅. Merged to main.

sasha: Filing a follow-up to add a linter rule that flags single-item only examples where the schema accepts arrays - helps prevent future confusion.
